newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Hapoalim chief attacks Israeli regulation.
newsitem.headline: Bank Hapoalim chief attacks Israeli regulation.

text.p: Bank Hapoalim chairman Emmanuel Sharon on Wednesday attacked Israeli banking regulation, saying it was out of sync with the world trend.
In the rest of the world banks are merging, noted the head of Israel's biggest bank at a management seminar in Tel Aviv.
"In this country the trend is a little different...it is to reduce the size of the banking group," he said. "The banking sector is out of sync and this in itself is problematic."

Recent reform in the sector requires Israel's powerful banks to significantly reduce their holdings in non-banking assets. The sector is dominated by five Israeli banks, only one of which is under complete private ownership.
Sharon faulted the government for failing to use U.S. loan guarantees to move to full shekel convertibility, which is necessary to enable the country to join world financial markets.
He also said that without peace Israel cannot integrate into the world economy.

"It is impossible not to remind the government that the critical condition for this integration is peace, he said. "To what extent will we be able to realise these conditions (liberalisation, peace) over the next four years, I don't know. I am not optimistic."

Issac Kaul, president of the state-controlled phone monopoly Bezeq Israel Telecom, said at the seminar that he did not believe the recent political tension in the Middle East was a major factor in the economy's current problems.
He added that in the telecommunications sector there was still interest from foreign investors.
He said the privatisation of Bezeq should be speeded up but added that the phone company was not in need of a strategic partner.
